situation:
You are the human resources communications manager at SUMMIT HOLLOW PARKS, a regional theme park operator with three parks and just over two thousand seasonal and year-round employees. The vice president of human resources (judge) has asked you to recommend how the company should deliver this season's performance review results, and to draft the message that carries the decision.

The founder built the parks over thirty years and is preparing to exit. A signed agreement to sell the company to a larger operator is expected to close in six weeks, and the buyer required that no company-wide communication touching pay, ratings, or job security go out before closing. Employees have not been told the sale is happening.

The year-round supervisors hold employment agreements of their own. Each one promises a written performance rating within two weeks of the season's close, with a written improvement plan attached to any rating below the standard. That deadline falls next week. Honoring it means sending rating letters during the window the buyer's agreement closed; honoring the buyer's agreement means the supervisors' letters arrive weeks late, after the merit increases those ratings set.

Sending the letters on schedule keeps the promise written into the supervisors' agreements, but breaks a term of the sale and could delay a closing the founder has asked the company to protect. Holding them keeps the sale clean, but a group of supervisors who were promised written ratings and timely merit increases will receive neither on time, and cannot be told why.

The vice president (judge) wants your recommendation on which obligation the company meets first and what the supervisors are told in writing. You will present it in the vice president's office. The vice president (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas. After you have presented and answered the vice president's questions, the vice president (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of vice president of human resources (judge) at SUMMIT HOLLOW PARKS, a regional theme park operator.

Business background is the same as the situation above. The year-round supervisors' employment agreements promise each of them a written rating within two weeks of the season's close, and that deadline falls next week.

You have asked the human resources communications manager (participant) to recommend which obligation the company meets first, what the supervisors are told in writing, and what format that message should take.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
